metadata.content: Mikey Lewis: I've earned my England Rugby League World Cup spot - 'We still have fighting chance' | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mikey Lewis: I've earned my England Rugby League World Cup spot - 'We still have fighting chance' England face Papua New Guinea in their final Rugby League World Cup pool fixture on Friday (9.05am kick-off), knowing they need a big win to keep their semi-final hopes alive; Mikey Lewis speaks to media after minimal participation at tournament so far Wednesday 28 October 2026 13:31, UK Image: England's Mikey Lewis spoke to media on Wednesday, saying he has 'earned' his Rugby League World Cup spot Mikey Lewis insists he has ‘earned’ his place in England’s Rugby League World Cup squad despite limited game time so far. The 2024 Man of Steel winner with Hull KR, Lewis struggled for form during the course of the 2026 Super League season, but was included in Brian McDermott's England squad for the World Cup. Yet the 25-year-old was left out of the matchday squad for England's opening 30-12 defeat to Tonga and was initially overlooked again for their second clash with France, before a late reshuffle saw him named on the bench. Lewis emerged for the final 20 minutes against the French, scoring two tries as part of a crushing 82-0 victory. For Friday's must-win contest against Papua New Guinea in Wollongong, Lewis has been named in the squad on the bench.
